name: aca-fl
title: Florida individual health plans, plan year 2026
summary: Read Florida's 2026 individual health plan data from CMS's public use files: rates, tobacco loads, rating and service areas, plan attributes, cost sharing and checks of the data itself.
description: Each task gives the AI extracts of CMS's public use files for Florida's individual health insurance market and states its facts in the question, such as an age, a rating area or a county. It asks for exact answers: a monthly rate, a tobacco load, a count, a list of plans or counties, or a finding in the data itself. Every field of the answer is checked, and a task passes only when all of them are right. Plan IDs, counts and lists must match exactly.

families.name: Rate lookup
families.what: The monthly rate of the right plan, rating area and age band, among plans with nearly the same name or ID.

families.name: Household total
families.what: A household's total as the sum of each person's listed rate, with tobacco users and the children's band.

families.name: Tobacco load
families.what: Tobacco loads that rise each year, step up by decade or stay flat, read at the right ages and for the right issuers.

families.name: Rating area
families.what: Which rating areas a plan is rated in, and how a county's plans relate to its rating area.

families.name: Service area
families.what: Which brands, networks and plans serve a county, joining service areas on the right key.

families.name: Plan attributes
families.what: Plan types, metal levels, networks and HSA eligibility, told apart across look-alike plans and variants.

families.name: Cost sharing
families.what: Deductibles, coinsurance and family amounts of the right plan and cost-sharing variant.

families.name: Joined files
families.what: Rates joined to plan attributes without counting a plan once per variant.

families.name: Counts
families.what: How many issuers, brands, plans and rows there are, counted at the right level.

families.name: Checking the data
families.what: Real oddities in the data, told apart from figures that only look wrong.
